text:
Pius Suter is the sort of middle-six forward every contender wants and nobody builds a marketing campaign around. Undrafted out of Zurich, he's played for Chicago, Detroit and Vancouver before landing in St. Louis, and he scores roughly what his chances say he should: five goals on 4.3 expected through 26 games.

The quiet part is the recent month. Two points in his last ten, even as the Blues won seven of those games, and his ice time has drifted up to almost 15 minutes a night. His line has been outshot at five on five (46.8% of attempts), and his relative numbers are negative. Some of that is bad luck, since St. Louis has scored 4.5 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had his value coming mostly from the penalty kill, with an adjusted offensive impact in the 87th percentile among forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found him on the end of passes across the slot more than most, which suits a player who finishes rather than creates. Watch whether the Blues' surge pulls his points back up toward his range of about 35 for the season.
